lesson: Today we work on one technique, the turn. The turn is the exact spot where the poem stops showing you a scene and starts telling you what it means. Most of this poem is a scene. You have the post-hole digger, smooth where you grip it, worn to the shape of use, and that honest weight that doesn't argue back. That is all picture. Then the poem shifts. The cool ground is still out there waiting, moves you from the tool in your hands to the work not yet done. That line points you outward and forward. This works because the picture came first. You feel the weight and the ache. So when the poem says the ground is waiting, you already want to go. Try this. Spend most of your poem on one physical scene. Then let one late line say what it is for. The second time, listen for how so up lands after that turn.
